purpose: Document separate English/local-language searches, first-party local registry/cadastre evidence, and bounded anonymous geometry discovery.
assessment: Official sources establish Dairut map products and a project-specific survey notice. Neither identifies a standing local property-registration/cadastre custodian for the ranked locator. The topographic index is not parcel geometry; city/local registry custody remains unconfirmed, and no parcel geometry was verified. No full parcel polygons or owner/address data were retained.
registryAssessment: The ESA topographic index is map-product evidence and the gazette notice is limited to a particular public-benefit survey project. No first-party Dairut registry office or general cadastral service was established. This does not prove that a local registry is absent.

officialPrimarySources.observation: Egyptian Survey Authority topographic index names Dairut among Assiut map centres and lists urban/village map scales. It is cartographic coverage evidence, not proof of a current cadastral registry for the town.

Official gazette publication describes a project-specific public-benefit survey notice at Dairut with display of project maps and compensation schedules. It does not establish a general town registry, parcel viewer, or current parcel coverage.

Official ESA institutional page describes the national survey authority and its mapping/ownership-record history. This national mandate does not locate a Dairut registry office or demonstrate WUP-point parcel coverage.
